benchmark_name: Expresso-AI: Explainable Video-Based Deep Learning Models for Depression Diagnosis
journal_venue: Published — 2023 11th International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII)
ground_truth_source: Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores from AVEC 2014 dataset (150 participants, 300 video recordings)
what_assessed_skills: Automatic depression severity prediction from facial videos; explainability/interpretability of deep video models via saliency maps, temporal attributions, region-wise attributions, and action unit cross-correlation
tasks_assessed: Depression severity regression from facial video clips; video-based saliency map generation; temporal attribution analysis; region-wise facial attribution analysis; action unit cross-correlation analysis
population_represented: 150 participants performing reading-aloud and freeform speech tasks (AVEC 2014); general adult population, no specific demographic breakdown reported
evaluation_method: Automated evaluation; models fine-tuned on AVEC 2014 facial video clips and evaluated on test set using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) against BDI-II ground truth scores; interpretability assessed via DeepLift attribution maps, Kendall Tau correlation with Action Units, and region-wise relevance pooling
llms_evaluated: None — paper evaluates deep convolutional video models (R3D, R(2+1)D, Wide ResNet), not LLMs
performance_scores: Best model R(2+1)D (Kinetics-700 + MiT, depth 50): MAE=6.626, RMSE=8.543; previous benchmark DepressNet-Full: MAE=6.60, RMSE=8.88
short_summary: This paper presents Expresso-AI, a framework for explainable automatic depression diagnosis (ADD) from facial videos using deep convolutional neural networks. The authors fine-tune ResNet-based 3D video architectures (R3D, R(2+1)D, Wide ResNet) pre-trained on large action recognition datasets on the AVEC 2014 depression dataset. The framework uses the DeepLift algorithm to generate attribution maps, enabling temporal, spatial, and region-wise interpretability of model decisions. Performance is evaluated via MAE and RMSE against BDI-II scores (Automated). The best model (R(2+1)D, Kinetics-700+MiT) achieves MAE=6.626 and RMSE=8.543, outperforming prior single-face benchmarks, and qualitative/quantitative analysis reveals correlations between specific facial action units (e.g., AU9, AU4) and depression severity levels.
